latest_nl_proof:
Fix the color c. Let S be the set of indices i in {1,2,3,4,5} such that at least one of A_i or B_i does not have color c. Equivalently, i is not in S exactly when both A_i and B_i have color c.

For each i in S, choose one point X_i from the pair {A_i,B_i} whose color is different from c; this is possible by definition of S. Because the ten points A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5 are pairwise distinct, the pairs {A_i,B_i} are disjoint from one another. Hence if i and j are distinct indices in S, then X_i and X_j are distinct points. Therefore the family {X_i : i in S} consists of |S| distinct points, all of color different from c.

So among the ten given points, there are at least |S| points whose color is different from c. By hypothesis, however, at most two of the ten points have color different from c. Hence |S| <= 2.

Now there are 5 total indices, so the complement {1,2,3,4,5} \ S has size at least 5 - 2 = 3. For every index i in this complement, neither A_i nor B_i has color different from c; equivalently, both A_i and B_i have color c.

Thus there exist at least three distinct indices i in {1,2,3,4,5} such that both A_i and B_i have color c, as required.
role_in_parent: Converts the large-circle bound from L1 into the existence of three support pairs whose two endpoints both have color c.
statement_nl: Let c be a fixed element of {red,green}. Consider five disjoint labeled pairs of points (A_1,B_1), (A_2,B_2), (A_3,B_3), (A_4,B_4), (A_5,B_5), and assume the ten points A_1,B_1,A_2,B_2,A_3,B_3,A_4,B_4,A_5,B_5 are pairwise distinct. If at most two of these ten points have color different from c, then there exist at least three distinct indices i in {1,2,3,4,5} such that both A_i and B_i have color c.

domain_restrictions: Each A_i and B_i is a point in some ambient universe of points
The ten points A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5 are pairwise distinct (equivalently: the five pairs are disjoint)
col maps each of these ten points to an element of {red,green}
"At most two of these ten points have color different from c" means |{p in {A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5} : col(p) != c}| <= 2
Indices i range over the finite set {1,2,3,4,5}
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all c in {red,green}, for all tuples of points (A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5) with the ten points pairwise distinct, for all colorings col: {A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5} -> {red,green}, if |{p in {A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5} : col(p) != c}| <= 2 then |{ i in {1,2,3,4,5} : col(A_i) = c and col(B_i) = c }| >= 3.
quantifier_order: forall c in {red,green} (c is an arbitrary fixed color)
forall tuples (A_1,B_1,...,A_5,B_5) of points satisfying pairwise distinctness / disjointness

variables.name: col
variables.role: coloring function assigning each of the ten points a color

witness_dependencies: The existentially asserted set of at least three indices I = {i in {1..5} : col(A_i) = c and col(B_i) = c} is determined (depends) on c, the ten points (A_i,B_i) and the coloring col.
One can take the witness set I to be the complement in {1..5} of S := { i : col(A_i) != c or col(B_i) != c }. Thus the choice of indices depends only on which pairs contain any point of color != c.
